rules.title: Utility Surcharge under Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords can get a special rent surcharge to cover rising heating and water costs, but the surcharge is capped based on the size of the building's total rent roll.
rules.key_value: 15% of rent roll (≤30 units); 5% (31-200 units); 3% (>200 units)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to apartment buildings subject to Newark rent control where heating/water costs rose more than 10% year over year.
rules.quoted_span: However, the increase allowed shall not exceed 15% of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain 30 or fewer units; and the increase allowed shall not exceed 5% of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain more than 30 units but less than 201 units; and, the increase allowed shall not exceed 3% of the monthly rent roll of apartments which contain more than 200 units.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: size of building rent roll (tiered caps by number of units)

rules.conflict_note: Ordinance amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I; text reflects amended version.

rules.title: New Construction Exemption from Rent Control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multi-unit dwellings are exempt from Newark's rent control rent-increase limits for up to 30 years after construction completion (or the length of the initial mortgage amortization, if shorter).
rules.key_value: Exemption for up to 30 years from completion of construction
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings that obtain a Certificate of Occupancy and file for the exemption with the Rent Control Board.
rules.quoted_span: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether building is newly constructed and has filed/received Certificate of Occupancy exemption from Rent Control Board

rules.conflict_note: Ordinance further amended 5-20-2026 by Ord. No. 6PSF-B.

rules.title: Substantial Rehabilitation / Vacancy Exemption from Rent Control
rules.requirement: A dwelling that has been vacant for at least 18 months (or was already vacant) and is substantially rehabilitated (cost exceeding 50% of its fair market value within 12 months) is exempt from Newark's rent increase restrictions for five years.
rules.key_value: 5-year exemption from rent restrictions after qualifying rehabilitation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to vacant dwellings substantially rehabilitated at a cost exceeding 50% of fair market value within a 12-month period, with Certificate of Occupancy and code compliance.
rules.quoted_span: Dwellings which become vacant and remain vacant for a minimum of 18 months or dwellings which are already vacant on the effective date of this section shall be exempt for a period of five years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge, if the Rent Control Board determines that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve-month period has exceeded 50% of the fair market value of the dwelling and that the dwelling has received a Certificate of Occupancy and meets all applicable State and municipal health and housing codes.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether unit was vacant 18+ months and substantially rehabilitated (cost >50% of fair market value)

rules.conflict_note: Ordinance amended 9-18-2024 and further 5-20-2026 by Ord. No. 6PSF-B.

rules.title: Rehabilitated Vacant Apartment Rent Increase
rules.requirement: A landlord who spends at least 12 months' worth of rent rehabilitating a vacant apartment may raise the rent on that unit by up to 10%, once per 12-month period.
rules.key_value: Max 10% increase, limited to one increase per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to individual vacant apartment units where the landlord has spent at least 12 months' actual rent on rehabilitation, subject to inspection and code compliance.
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord that rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending a total amount equal to at least 12 months of actual monthly rent per unit will be entitled to a maximum of 10% increase in the actual monthly rent.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether landlord spent at least 12 months' rent rehabilitating the vacant unit
